text:
Maya H: Quick sync — I'm mapping TTFT / tok/s to SLOs for the hosted API. Question: do we want per-model SLOs or per-route SLOs? Also, we'll need fresh bench runs to validate thresholds. Anybody owning the bench side?

Jon P: Per-route for user-facing variance (chat vs embeddings). Model-level SLOs as a fallback baseline. Don't create too many SLOs though — keep it actionable.

Rachel L: +1 per-route. We should track first-token TTFT and token throughput separately. Proposal: p95_first_token < 400ms for interactive routes; p95_token_throughput >= target depending on model class. Need data to pick numbers.

Maya H: Good call. @Kevin S can you run microbenches for redwood-xl and gpt-medium (seq_len=512) and return p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and tok/s? Perf-bot, can you schedule a job as backup?

perf-bot: Scheduled perf job #4521. Params: requests=1000, seq_len=512, concurrency_sweep=[1,4,8], models=[gpt-medium,redwood-xl], collect=[ttft_ms, tok_per_s]. ETA ~45m.

Kevin S: I'll do a quick local run first to sanity-check. Can someone paste the CI bench command / YAML? I want to align flags (flamegraph on, sample collection).

Jon P: Use this snippet: ```bash
./bench --model redwood-xl --seq 512 --concurrency 4 --requests 1000 --collect=ttft,throughput --perf-flags="--flamegraph"
``` Also add `--trace-sample-rate=0.05` for sample-level percentiles.

Kevin S: Thanks. Kicking off now. I'll upload logs to /mnt/perf/18645/ and ping when flamegraphs + CSVs are ready.

Rachel L: For the dashboard: can we add a panel that shows p95 TTFT by route with a traffic-weight overlay? That way we prioritize SLOs where latency hurts most users.

Maya H: Agreed. @Anshuman can you add a runtime dashboard panel? A heatmap of p50/p95/p99 by route would help.

Anshuman: Yup. I need the query form — do we compute percentiles over raw samples or use our aggregated stream (exp-decay)? The former is more accurate but heavier.

Maya H: Prefer sample-level percentiles from traces: use `percentile(95, trace.ttft_ms) by route`. If that's too expensive for dashboard refresh, fallback to the exp-decay aggregates we already emit. Add a legend note about method.

Jon P: Also call out cache-warm state. Cold prefix/KV cache can skew TTFT: annotate panel or add split line for warm vs cold.

Kevin S: Run finished. Initial numbers (conc=4): redwood-xl p95_first_token = 390ms, p99 ~ 620ms; tok/s median ~ 42, p95_tok/s ~ 38. Spike observed at conc=8 — queue latency visible. Uploading artifacts now.

Maya H: Excellent. Paste the flamegraph + raw CSV link here so Rachel can use it for SLO proposal.

Kevin S: Link: https://perf.internal/redwood/18645/bench-4521 — flamegraph + raw CSV uploaded. Key note: queuing starts >6 concurrency for this model; kernel sched delays visible in flamegraph.

Rachel L: Thanks. I'll draft a short SLO proposal doc: baseline per-route p95_first_token=400ms, per-model p95_tok/s thresholds in a table (will reference bench CSV). Will open PR in docs repo and tag runtime team.

Maya H: Sounds good. If no objections, we'll lock defaults in 48h and start adding dashboard alerts for regressions. :thumbsup:

Jon P: SGTM. One follow-up: include sample sizes in dashboard tooltips so we don't act on noisy percentiles.

Anshuman: Added note. I'll put panel in runtime dashboard and mark it draft.

Kevin S: Thanks — happy to rerun with different seq_len or patch builds if needed.

Maya H: Great coordination, team. We'll close once PR and dashboard draft are up.
